analysis.title: Oil's $27 War Premium Is Gone: Goldman Says That's Exactly Why You Should Own Commodities In 2027
key_insights: Goldman estimates the Brent risk premium fell from $27 on the Friday before the midterms to only a few dollars in recent days. Goldman attributes the November energy and copper selloff to sentiment and lower Mideast escalation risk, not physical fundamentals.

Goldman argues the lower risk premium raises the hedging and diversification value of commodities by offering a more attractive entry point. Its base case of further energy moderation implies about -1% BCOM total return through end-2027, after +26% in 2026 (energy +110% YTD).

Persian Gulf crude exports, including 'dark' barrels, recovered to near 2025 levels by September, and the global oil market likely flipped back into surplus in October. Goldman expects Mideast oil output to average 1.1mb/d above 2025 in 2027.

Adaptation has worked for crude but not for refined products, LNG, aluminium feedstock and fertilizer. Gulf exports of these remain well below pre-war levels because refineries, smelters and liquefaction trains hit in strikes are not fully repaired.

Tanker workarounds account for about 3/4 of the ~$20/bbl y/y rise in the global average crude freight rate, from a Hormuz war-risk premium, a smaller effective fleet and the US blockade sidelining Iran's fleet. Product tankers switching to crude is lifting product freight, which largely passes through to pump prices.
Goldman sees three factors favoring long commodities as a portfolio hedge: upside risk to energy prices, high sensitivity of stocks and bonds to energy prices, and upside risk to agricultural prices.

Escalation scenario: Brent could exceed $130 in early 2027 and average about $120 if Gulf output stays 2.5mb/d below 2025 (versus 1.1mb/d above in the base case). US wholesale diesel could reach about $230 if another 3mb/d of refining is knocked out.
The Nov 1 upside scenario had Brent at $140 and averaging $130 in 2027 with the Gulf 3.5mb/d short, so the tail narrowed. The 2027 base case for Brent is unchanged at $88.

TTF: Goldman's 2027 average of 45 EUR/MWh is 34% below the forward curve. Its Q1 scenario grid runs from 41 to 147 against forwards at 85, and the probability of the low winter supply scenario was cut to 30% from 45% after a jump in Mideast LNG exports. TTF could approach 150 EUR/MWh in Q1 if Gulf LNG exports are 25-30% of pre-war levels and the winter is 0.7°C colder than normal.

Since the Iran war began, the 6-month rolling correlation of daily changes between Brent and 10-year Treasury yields reached about 0.5, and Brent's correlation with the S&P 500 fell to about -0.45 (approximate, read off a chart). The 1-month Brent-yield correlation has been negative since late September as AI/risk-asset volatility became the bigger driver.

Goldman expects a renewed energy supply shock in 2027 to lower bond prices (as in 2026) and equities (as in 2022). In every 12-month period over six decades when both equities and bonds had negative real returns, gold or broader commodities delivered positive real returns.

BCOM Agriculture is up 10% YTD. Upside risks cited: Hormuz-linked fertilizer trade (typically 1/3 of global fertilizer exports), Black Sea grain (15-20% of global grain trade), biofuel diversion, and an El Niño forecast to be the strongest on record. West African cocoa (~65% of global exports) and Vietnamese robusta are most exposed.

Hedge trades: long June 2027 European gasoline (EBOB), with a 20% expected return in the base case, 62% under renewed escalation and a 4% loss in the most bearish scenario; and 27Q1 TTF call spreads. Longer term, Goldman likes puts on TTF Summer 2029 as the 2025-26 LNG FID wave arrives after 2027.

Goldman sees LME copper at $15,600/t by Dec27, 13% above spot, on US tariff ambiguity pulling metal into US stockpiles and China's scrap-invoicing crackdown pushing fabricators to refined cathode. It sees aluminium falling to $2,600 on abundant bauxite and Indonesian smelters (about 4% of global output by end-2027 from 1% at end-2025). It recommends long Dec27 copper, short Dec27 aluminium.

Goldman cut its Dec27 gold target to $4,650/toz from $4,800 (itself cut from $5,400 a week earlier) because economists now expect a third 25bp Warsh hike in March 2027 on top of December's. The target is 16% above spot. Goldman expects private investors to return once the Fed starts easing in December 2027, and central bank buying remains the floor.

Other desks lean bearish on oil: JPMorgan estimated a global oil surplus of about 1.4mb/d in October, and Morgan Stanley flagged Dated Brent below the nearby futures contract, a sign of a soft physical market (per Reuters). Goldman's base case already assumes a surplus and argues the hedge case rests on the tails.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman argues the lower risk premium makes commodities a cheaper hedge against stock-and-bond drawdowns, although base case total returns are near zero.

Abundant bauxite and new Indonesian smelter capacity push the market into surplus and price to $2,600.
Target cut again to $4,650/toz on expected Fed hikes, with central bank buying as the floor.

trade_ideas.rationale: Refiners shifted output from gasoline to diesel and jet, leaving gasoline tighter than it looks, and low gasoline margins leave room for sharp upside if refining is hit again.
trade_ideas.risk: Most bearish scenario implies a 4% loss.

trade_ideas.rationale: Cheap way to hedge a tight European winter after the risk premium liquidation, with low inventories and a risk of cold weather plus an LNG outage.

trade_ideas.rationale: Copper supply is tight while aluminium faces a surplus, and the pair is more immune to an AI-cycle turn or more Fed hikes than an outright long.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman says the risk premium dropped from $27 to a few dollars while fundamentals for products, LNG and freight remain tight, so long commodity hedges are cheaper. Escalation could send Brent above $130.
tension_points.bear_case: JPMorgan estimates a 1.4mb/d October surplus and Morgan Stanley sees Dated Brent below futures, which points to a soft physical market. Goldman's own base case is $88 Brent and -1% BCOM returns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A lasting diplomatic breakthrough in the Gulf, or Gulf output recovering well above 2025 levels, would undercut the hedge case. Goldman flags the pickup in tanker attacks near Hormuz as the risk to its supply base case.

tension_points.bull_case: Low European inventories plus a cold snap and an LNG outage could push TTF toward 150 EUR/MWh against forwards at 85.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman's 2027 TTF base case is 45 EUR/MWh, 34% below forwards, and the low winter supply scenario probability fell to 30% from 45% on higher Mideast LNG exports.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Gulf LNG exports recovering above 25-30% of pre-war levels this winter and a normal or warm winter.
